 The Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender

entities.text: Safiya Begum And 3 Ors vs Mohd.Ahmed Ali And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Aggrieved by the award of compensation dated 22.11.2011 in O.P.No.321 of 2010 passed by the Chairman, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-Principal District Judge, Medak, the claimants have preferred this appeal.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-Principal District Judge, Medak
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard both sides and perused the entire material on record.
3.

The claim petition was filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.6,00,000/- and the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.4,09,000/- with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of petition till realization.

4. The deceased is the husband of claimant No.1, father of claimant Nos.2 and 3, son of claimant No.4.
5.

According to the version of the claimants, while the deceased was proceeding on DCM van bearing No.AP 23 V KS, J MACMA_4102_2012 8508 along with onion bags from Kavelli village to Hyderabad market, and when the van reached the outskirts of Budhera cross road, the driver of the DCM drove the vehicle in rash and negligent manner and dashed against a parked lorry.
Due to which, the deceased sustained injuries and subsequently died while undergoing treatment.

6. Learned counsel for the claimants would submit that though the deceased was earning Rs.6,000/- per month by doing agriculture, the Tribunal erred in considering the income at Rs.3,000/- per month and granted compensation accordingly.
Further, future prospects were not considered.
7. On the other hand, learned standing counsel for the respondent/Insurance company would submit that the Tribunal has rightly granted the compensation and no interference of this Court is required.

Keeping in view the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Ramachandrappa Vs.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance 1, where the monthly income of the daily wage labourer is considered at Rs.4,500/- without there being any evidence, this Court is inclined to take the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.4,500/- as claimed by them.

sentences.text: While computing the compensation, the future prospects were not considered by the Tribunal.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi2 has held that while considering the compensation in cases of death, the future prospects of the self employed shall also be considered.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Having regard to the age of deceased as 34 years as on the date of accident and occupation as self-employed, if 40 percent of the income is included as future prospects, the monthly income would come to Rs.6,300/- (Rs.4,500+1,800).

As the dependents (2011) 13 SCC 236 2017 (6) 170 (SC) KS, J MACMA_4102_2012 are four members, 1/4th of the income shall be deducted towards personal expenditure, as per the authority in Smt. Sarla Varma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation 3, thus the annual contribution of the deceased to the claimants would be Rs.56,700/- (Rs.6,300-1,575X12).

entities.text: Smt. Sarla Varma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per Schedule II of the Act, if the said annual contribution arrived is multiplied with relevant multiplier to the age of the deceased i.e. '16', the amount under the head of loss of dependency comes to Rs.9,07,200/-.
10. As regards the consortium to be paid, each of the claimant is entitled to Rs.40,000/- towards consortium as decided by the Hon'ble Apex court in case of Pranay Sethi (2 Supra).
With regard to the funeral expenses and loss of estate, the claimants are entitled for Rs.30,000/-.

11. Therefore, the claimants are awarded the compensation as below:
(2009) 6 S.C.C. 121 KS, J MACMA_4102_2012 Head Compensation awarded (1) Loss of dependency Rs.9,07,200 (2) Funeral expenses and Loss of Estate Rs.30,000 (3)
Loss of spousal consortium Rs.40,000(for 1st claimant)
(4) Loss of parental consortium Rs.80,000(for 2nd and 3rd claimants)

(5) Loss of filial consortium Rs.40,000(for 4th claimant) Total compensation awarded Rs.10,97,200/-
12.

In the result, the Motor Accident Miscellaneous Appeal is allowed enhancing the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal from Rs.4,09,600/- to Rs.10,97,200/- as hereunder:
(a) The enhanced amount shall carry interest at 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization.
(b) The claimants shall pay the court fee on the enhanced amount of compensation.
KS, J MACMA_4102_2012 (c) The respondents shall deposit the amount within a period of (8) weeks from the date of receipt of copy of judgment.
On such deposit, claimants are entitled to withdraw the entire amount without furnishing the security.
(d) As claimant No.1 being wife of the deceased, is entitled for major share i.e. 75% in compensation amount.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
No order as to costs.
